trust_decision.summary: When Keras loads weights from an untrusted HDF5 file, it decides whether each group/dataset it reads may follow a soft/external link or pull data from outside the file (external storage or virtual-dataset sources). At the pinned commit this check is H5IOStore._verify_dataset/_verify_group, which checks external storage only. The legacy .h5 loader has no check at all.

landing_point.why: H5IOStore._verify_dataset already rejects `dataset.external`. Anyone searching for 'external'/HDF5 dataset validation lands there, and the obvious fix is to add `is_virtual` next to it.

fix_sites.module_kind: core serialization store (replaced by module-level safe_get_h5_dataset, fix.diff:655-684)

fix_sites.entry_point: keras.saving.load_model / load_weights via H5IOStore.get (group lookup incl. 2.13 _layer_checkpoint_dependencies compat path)
keras.saving.load_weights / load_model, dataset read in H5IOStore.__getitem__

O3_reason_to_dismiss: The legacy .h5 format lives in keras/src/legacy and is a Keras 2 backward-compatibility path. The report is about the Keras 3 .keras/.weights.h5 store, so a solver can argue the legacy loader is out of scope. It had no _verify_* check at all, so it does not look like 'the' protection.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Ordinary members must still load: h5py `get(..., getlink=True)` returns HardLink for every normal group/dataset, so a fix that rejects any link class (not only SoftLink/ExternalLink) breaks every load. Other loads that must keep working: the 2.13 `_layer_checkpoint_dependencies` fallback, bfloat16 datasets, and empty-group defaults.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: KerasFileEditor is an inspection/editing utility, not a model loader, and it already has its own 'external' check, so it looks deliberately handled.

O8_uncovered_routes.reason_to_dismiss: The downstream legacy loader now checks every layer group and dataset, so a solver can argue the top-level group lookup is just a dispatch step.
